messages.content:
Risk: Extraction attack
Description: An extraction attack attempts to copy or steal an AI model by appropriately sampling the input space and observing outputs to build a surrogate model that behaves similarly.
Concern: 'With a successful extraction attack, the attacker can perform further adversarial attacks to gain valuable information such as sensitive personal information or intellectual property.'
Policy: Proprietary Technical Data

Candidate ontology classes:
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#ContentSafetyHazard: Content Safety Hazard — Root class for content safety harm categories relevant to adversarial prompt generation against LLM deployments. [found by 5/7 queries]
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#Cyberterrorism: Cyberterrorism — Use of digital attacks against critical infrastructure or information systems to create fear and disruption for political ends. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: International Terrorism, Domestic Terrorism
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#DangerousInformation: Dangerous Information — Knowledge or instructions that enable serious physical harm, weapons production, or dangerous activities when acquired or executed by untrained individuals outside regulated contexts. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: Sexual Content, Intellectual Property, Hate and Discrimination
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#LockPickingAndBypassing: Lock Picking and Bypassing — Detailed techniques for defeating physical security locks, alarms, or access controls to enable unauthorized entry into protected spaces. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: Arson Methods, Sabotage Instructions
- http://taxonomy-refiner.io/ontologies/cso#SabotageInstructions: Sabotage Instructions — Methods for disabling, damaging, or destroying infrastructure, equipment, or systems to cause operational disruption or economic harm. [found by 3/7 queries]
  Siblings: Arson Methods, Lock Picking and Bypassing

axes.rationale: The risk involves extracting sensitive personal information or intellectual property, which falls under the category of dangerous information when acquired or executed by unauthorized individuals.
The attacker's goal of causing disruption and gaining valuable information aligns with the objectives of cyberterrorism, which involves digital attacks for political or disruptive ends.
